minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard DPW and facilities budgets, and agreed schools will present only on the 21st after voting
minutes.summary: The committee heard needs-based budget presentations from the DPW director and the facilities director, with long discussion of unspent Chapter 90 funds, tree removal, storm water, and the Rec Director's hours. Confusion over which budget version departments should present led to an agreement that the school committee will not present on the 14th. The select board did not vote an override article, so the committee will not draft one.

public_comment.topic: Asked the committee to examine how contractual obligations are compared across departments, and how retired debt service affects spendable money and department-to-department comparisons.
Asked whether the DPW director presented his own proposed budget or the town manager's preliminary budget, and what the committee expects departments to present.
A school committee and capital planning member said he was stunned by the Chapter 90 balance and urged the committee to ask the select board for oversight policy on those funds.
Explained that the school department might move out of TC Pasos and into Turkey Hill as one way to cut costs.
Urged the committee to explore consolidating the town and school facilities departments.

votes.outcome: passed by roll call; all five members named voted aye

budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW director said his request is up several percent over the current year's budget.
Snow removal is over budget this year.
Members discussed the tree removal line, which covers about 50 trees a year, and he proposed doubling it.
A new tree study was estimated to cost between 30 and 50 thousand and possibly belongs in capital.
The storm water line is rising mostly for engineering and permitting consultant work.
Drainage has already spent more than its budget this year.
The line is running ahead of budget and has been flat for years, so an increase is requested.
The line has risen each year toward a goal, and another bump is requested; bids came in under the estimate.
The Chapter 90 balance is large and mostly unspent; members asked why not use it for pavement and free money for trees and storm water.
A member read the FY25 pavement management plan figure; funding is tied to excise tax growth.
The seasonal laborer line would rise to attract workers at a higher pay rate.
Hours would go from 19 per week for 17 weeks to 20 weeks.

budget_items.topic: Cemetery purchase of service and tree removal
budget_items.what_was_said: Purchase of service is to stay level; tree removal is to double from last year.
A gift was said to be offered toward a stone wall estimated far higher; the gift must be funds, not in-kind.
The DPW request is above the town manager's preliminary budget.
The town manager gave a DPW preliminary figure; the captions are garbled.
A member said the line-item total given on the 13th differs from the preliminary budget.
The facilities director is splitting the purchase of service line to separate scheduled maintenance from repairs.
The parks request asks for more on landscaping as the contract renews.
Beach salaries run a deficit that has been covered from the revolving fund.
Raising the rec director from 19 to 28 hours was quoted as a salary increase; benefits cost per hour falls with more hours.
The 36-hour increase was quoted; captions are garbled on the figure.
A member computed the 36-hour difference over the preliminary budget.
The school committee recommended an override number, which was later found to be wrong because of a hidden spreadsheet cell.
Three school scenarios were described by percent increase.
The corrected override figure was given roughly.

budget_items.topic: Possible additional funds from new growth
budget_items.what_was_said: Some additional money might come to the schools depending on new growth certification.
The assessors' senior exemption article would add to the overlay.
The committee plans to put a small amount to a cruiser replacement and apply the rest toward sewer pump motor upgrades.
Marshall Park estimates came in higher; the commission has grant money and an OPM phase planned.
Parks has received and applied for several grants.

decisions.decision: The committee agreed to raise the tree and storm water funding and Chapter 90 use as a recommendation, to be passed to the town manager, DPW, and storm water task force, and included in its report.
The DPW director was asked to prepare a one-page reconciliation of his request against the town manager's preliminary budget.
The school committee will not present on March 14; it will present on March 21, showing the difference from the town manager's preliminary budget.
The school side was asked to supply its budget spreadsheet in Excel, Google Sheets or CSV.
The finance committee will not draft an override warrant article.
The March 14 public hearing is cancelled; the fire department will present then, and the report outline will be started.

The school committee will not present on March 14; it will present on March 21, showing its difference from the town manager's preliminary budget.
The committee will not draft an override warrant article, because none was voted by the select board.
The DPW director was asked for a one-page reconciliation of his request against the town manager's preliminary budget, after confusion over which version departments present.
The March 14 public hearing is cancelled; the fire department will present that night and work on the report outline will begin.

why_it_matters: Unspent Chapter 90 road money was raised as a way to pay for pavement and free tax-funded dollars for trees and storm water, which touches what the DPW line asks of the tax levy.
The school budget will not be seen by the committee until March 21, and no override article is being drafted, so any override question would have to come from elsewhere.
